state.assignment_rule: Any tier that breaks a measured dimension for a class leaves the race. The survivors order by combined load: interface size, package weight, and cost per call. The catalogue takes ties only when the surface serves many apps generically. The companion must prove matching auth and release behavior. Where no tier owns complete evidence, the class returns to preparation; no tier is granted by default.
state.class_chart: Widget C paints a bar chart of invoice totals, picks one bar, and tears down. The adapter build offers 3 synchronous calls, 3 failure leaves, a single callback under 4 dispatch rules (one dispatch at a time, sealed failure notes, synchronous reentrant update, teardown inside a callback), deep frozen copies wherever values cross, opaque tokens, repeatable teardown, 279 lines, and a 6051-byte bundle before real SDK weight. The companion build offers render, select, and release inside typed envelopes, 7 failure leaves, no callbacks at all, frozen bytes plus a table per render, repeatable release, reads after release expire, a pinned 209-byte render request with a 164-byte reply, 360 lines, and a 20236-byte bundle holding 11041 shared policy bytes. The workflow clears on both tiers; the adapter answers selection locally while the companion holds SDK weight outside the audited browser asset. Catalogue sketch: slim vendor-neutral chart calls with the renderer pinned per release, viable only once charts turn into platform surface; assembly from present operations fails for lack of canvas and SVG primitives.
state.class_clipboard: Op B moves text between the app and the device clipboard across an async platform call guarded by permissions. The adapter build offers 2 async calls, 4 failure leaves, an upfront permission check that closes on denial, a stated no-ordering rule under concurrency, no callbacks, 156 lines, and a 2987-byte bundle. The companion build offers a server pastebin cell inside typed envelopes, 9 failure leaves, pinned 106-byte read and 127-byte write requests, 301 lines, and a 16768-byte bundle holding shared policy weight. The finding: server cell and device cell never meet, so the companion misses the device-clipboard workflow and drops the compare-targets dimension. Catalogue sketch: 2 generic calls with 4 errors, viable after a live permission-matrix pass plus demand from a second app.
state.class_storage: Op A keeps string keys and values in a synchronous platform store bounded by quota and origin rules. The adapter build offers 3 synchronous calls, 3 failure leaves, no callbacks, no copy crossings, an availability gate that never touches the host when closed, 184 lines, and a 4559-byte bundle. The companion build offers 3 async calls, 8 failure leaves, strict JSON envelopes with a pinned 117-byte get, 132-byte set, and 72-byte reply, destination plus auth checks per call, 334 lines, and an 18360-byte bundle holding 11041 shared policy bytes. The workflow clears on both tiers; companion storage lives server-side, shifting offline behavior, latency, and cross-device reach. Catalogue sketch: 3 generic calls with 3 errors, viable once another shipped app wants origin-local persistence.
state.constraints: No outside users exist, so compatibility binds nothing. The catalogue admits only through the compiler plus distribution review, and vendor-named operations stay out forever. Network calls follow the destination allowlist while credentials travel as environment names absent from every log. Browser views append at the root alone, and teardown poisons handles while discarding late callbacks. A second vendor must integrate with zero vendor-specific compiler edits.
state.experiment: X-R01-1 scores three integration tiers within each class once the shared-controls library proof landed: generic catalogue growth, reviewed adapter package, and companion service. Every class drove an identical workflow through a host-injected adapter build and a typed-envelope companion build resting on the shared outbound policy. Browsers stayed unlaunchable, so native-call trust comes from cited platform specifications pending live confirmation. Six builds total 1638 lines behind 54 green legs, and each bundle rebuilds to identical bytes.
